classification.difficultyReason: Use right-triangle trigonometry, tangent symmetry and complementary central angles to calculate minor and major arc lengths.

content.prompt:
$AC$ and $AD$ are equal tangents to the circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$.

The point $A$ is $13\text{ cm}$ from the centre $B$.

$BC$ is perpendicular to $AC$ and $BD$ is perpendicular to $AD$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle centred at B with external point A to the right, tangents AC and AD, radii BC and BD, horizontal BA labelled 13, four vertex dots and perpendicular markers at C and D. Tangency points and perpendicular markers are derived from the radius-to-distance ratio.
spec.mathematics: Radius 5 cm; BA = 13 cm; BC perpendicular to AC and BD perpendicular to AD. Coordinates use radius 1, A = (13/5,0), C = (5/13,12/13), D = (5/13,-12/13).
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and geometric relationships are visible; no calculated angles or arc lengths.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $\angle ABC$ in radians, to 3 d.p.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle ABC&=\frac{5}{13}\\\angle ABC&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\\angle ABC&\approx1.176\text{ radians}.\end{align*}$$

The right triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ are congruent, so $BA$ bisects the minor central angle $CBD$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CBD&=2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\l_{\text{minor}}&=r\theta\\l_{\text{minor}}&=5\times2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\l_{\text{minor}}&\approx11.76\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

The major and minor arcs together form the circumference.
$$\begin{align*}l_{\text{major}}&=2\pi r-l_{\text{minor}}\\l_{\text{major}}&=10\pi-10\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)\\l_{\text{major}}&\approx19.66\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
